label: <DEL> delimiter step (stronger for long sequences)
explanation: Fires mainly on the <DEL> delimiter step, which holds 91% of activation mass. It is active on only about 54% of delimiter steps. Longer sequences make firing more likely: restricting to L >= 6 raises precision from 0.54 to 0.64, and L >= 7 to 0.72. The first original token also modulates it: firing is more common when the first token is g/o/t/k/y/2/3/e (precision 0.84 on those). The remaining ~8% of mass is weak firing in the last few original-phase steps of long sequences, mostly on first occurrences of f/i/u/s/b/v/d; these often build up just before <DEL>. Almost silent in the copy phase (0.8% of mass, mostly the step after <DEL>) and on the first two steps.
